bugs.what: Item-use menu options (e.g. 'use a sealed letter') sometimes occupied the same numbered slot a movement/action option had held on a previous page, causing an accidental read instead of an intended move.

'travel to a known place' only lists major landmarks, not every visited room, so backtracking through multi-room dungeons/wilderness (e.g. the Ashwood, Fenmarch fens, Cinderhall mine) required long manual step-by-step retracing even after the area was fully mapped.

Several 'settle the disagreement between companions' will-checks (DC 11-12) failed repeatedly despite a decent +3 will modifier, with no way to see the odds skew before spending the only attempt available per visit; failures dinged two companions' regard at once with no real recourse.
bugs.where: companion dialogue after settling a hold's grief

confusions: It's not obvious early on that 'get your bearings' / 'weigh what this grief asks' are free scouting actions worth using proactively before committing to a resolution path for a hold's grief.
The pagination ('p1/2', 'more in this room') sometimes reshuffled which numbered option meant what between pages, making rapid play (picking by number) occasionally misfire.

It wasn't clear until using status/weigh whether a given item (e.g. Keeper's Key, Prior's rite, founding ledger) was the intended key to a specific locked door versus flavor loot, requiring a lot of experimentation.
suggestions: Let 'travel to a known place' optionally show recently-passed-through minor rooms too, or add a 'retrace last path' shortcut for wilderness/dungeon crawls.
Show the numeric roll odds consistently in the menu text before a risky companion-mediation check, and/or let a failed mediation be retried once per visit like other skill checks.
Keep action numbering stable across 'more in this room' pagination so repeat-key play doesn't misfire into the wrong action.
A brief on-pickup tooltip confirming an item's intended use ('this opens X') would reduce trial-and-error for key items.
